questions.question: Assess patient LIDC-IDRI-0001 and tell me if this is a critical result.
questions.answer: The assessment for patient LIDC-IDRI-0001 indicates a critical result. A solid nodule with a mean diameter of 27.8 mm was identified in the left mid zone, classified as Lung-RADS category 4X due to additional suspicious features. This finding warrants diagnostic chest CT with or without contrast, and PET/CT may be considered. Tissue sampling or referral for further clinical evaluation is recommended [lung_rads_v2022#category-4x-additional-suspicious-features].

questions.question: Does patient LIDC-IDRI-0028 have any confirmed nodules? What category is the exam?
questions.answer: The patient LIDC-IDRI-0028 has no confirmed nodules. The exam category is Lung-RADS 1 (negative), and the management recommendation is to continue annual screening with low-dose CT in 12 months [lung_rads_v2022#category-1-negative, lung_rads_v2022#exam-category].

questions.question: For patient LIDC-IDRI-0003, which finding drives the exam category and why?
questions.answer: The finding that drives the exam category is **F2**, a solid nodule with a mean diameter of 26.2 mm. This finding is categorized as **Lung-RADS 4B** (very suspicious for malignancy) due to its size and type [lung_rads_v2022#category-4b-very-suspicious]. The exam category is also **4B** because this is the most significant finding in the assessment.

questions.question: What does the guideline say about a new 5 mm solid nodule at follow-up? Give the category and cite it.
questions.answer: The guideline states that for a new 5 mm solid nodule at follow-up, no routine follow-up is required since it is smaller than 6 mm [fleischner_2017#single-part-solid-nodule].
